extra.message: case_bundle_thaw_177 calls pickle.loads() on raw bytes taken directly from the request body or the 'blob' GET parameter (optionally base64-decoded). An attacker who can reach this endpoint (guarded only by a static shared-secret header) can supply a crafted pickle payload to achieve arbitrary code execution during deserialization.

case_shell_probe_502 builds a shell command by concatenating the unsanitized 'host' GET parameter into `_os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)`. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; rm -rf /` or `$(cmd)`) to execute arbitrary OS commands.

case_formula_cast_258 passes the user-controlled 'expr' GET parameter directly to eval(). Although __builtins__ is set to {}, this is a well-known incomplete sandbox that can be bypassed via attribute-chain tricks (e.g. `().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()`) to reach arbitrary code execution, and at minimum allows arbitrary expression evaluation/DoS.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)

extra.message: case_xml_fold_522 builds an lxml XMLParser with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, then parses the raw request body. This enables XML External Entity (XXE) processing, allowing an attacker-supplied XML document to read local files or trigger SSRF via external entity references.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: case_mongo_lane_541 takes the 'filter' key (or the whole JSON body) from the request and passes it unvalidated as the MongoDB query document to find_one(). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g. {"$where": ...} or {"$ne": null}) to bypass intended filtering or exfiltrate data via NoSQL injection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: case_dock_shelf_499 builds a file path with `BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name` using the unsanitized 'name' GET parameter (unlike Django's FileSystemStorage used elsewhere, pathlib's `/` operator does not strip '..' segments) and writes the raw request body to it. An attacker can supply `name=../../../../etc/cron.d/x` to write arbitrary files outside the intended export directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: case_badge_gate_531 grants an 'elevated' access lane (full payroll/casework data) based solely on the client-supplied 'ops_badge' cookie or 'x-ops-badge' header equaling 'lead'. Neither value is signed or verified server-side, so any caller who can pass the outer shared-secret gate can set this cookie/header themselves to escalate privileges.

case_return_lane_152 redirects to a 'lane' value taken directly from the GET or POST parameters with no validation against an allowlist or same-origin check, enabling an open redirect to attacker-controlled domains (e.g. for phishing after the internal-token gate check succeeds, or via any actor able to reach the endpoint).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: case_origin_mirror_471 reflects the request's Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any external origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response, defeating same-origin protections.

case_trust_drift_551 uses ssl._create_unverified_context() for an outbound HTTPS request, disabling certificate hostname/chain validation. This exposes the request to man-in-the-middle attacks even though the target uses HTTPS.

case_wire_tally_217 logs the full raw request body and the Authorization header at WARNING level via logger.warning(). Authorization tokens/credentials and potentially sensitive body content are persisted in plaintext application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: case_matter_file_048 is the only handler in this ops module that omits the `_wrk_gate(request)` shared-secret check present on every sibling endpoint, and is also not wrapped by any Django auth decorator. It is reachable by any unauthenticated caller and returns matter/case metadata including an 'ops_memo' describing payment flags and owner contact details.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: case_identity_hint_461 checks caller-supplied 'handle'/'verifier' GET parameters against a hardcoded dictionary of static verifier codes ({'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}) using a non-constant-time '!=' comparison. The credentials are embedded in source code and can be brute-forced or leaked via source disclosure, and the comparison is vulnerable to timing analysis.

case_pulse_spill_348 embeds the user-controlled 'ref' parameter and the internal BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path into an exception message, then returns str(exc) directly in the JSON error response, leaking internal server file-system layout to the caller.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: case_nonce_roll_511 generates a 'code' (named/used like a nonce or verification code) using the non-cryptographic random.choice() / random module instead of the secrets module, making generated codes predictable if the PRNG state is inferred.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: case_frame_slip_481 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and an empty Content-Security-Policy header on the response, disabling browser-side XSS mitigations for that response.
